$comment: Measured tuning constants. Generated by scripts/calibration/analyse.py from scripts/calibration/data/measurements.ndjson — do not edit by hand. build.rs turns this into compile-time constants, so a value here is the value the estimator uses, and `evidence` is what it rests on.

baseline_offset.$comment: Per-architecture correction to the process baseline, in bytes. The layer-count model leaves a residual that is architecture-shaped and reproducible; this charges it where it is positive. `default` is zero, since an unmeasured architecture has no evidence either way.

checkpoint_headroom_bytes.$comment: What a real prompt adds over the campaign's probe, by architecture, from llama.cpp's context checkpoints. Reserved as slop rather than charged to the correction: a service that never sees a long prompt would otherwise read as a large over-reservation and clamp unreachably.

compute_buffer_curves.$comment: Ordered: the first entry whose arch list contains the model's architecture wins, so a variant-guarded entry must precede the general one for the same arch. `slope_scales_with_ubatch` is true throughout: the context term is calibrated at ubatch 512 and the measured compute buffer is proportional to batch — Magidonia takes 388 MiB at ub 512 and 1552 at 2048, exactly four times, and Qwen3.6-27B 290 and 1160 — so a flat slope under-reserves at any larger batch. At the default batch this changes nothing.

default.evidence: least-squares fit of max per-run average (compute + unaccounted) / n_gpus to base + base_batch + slope*(ctx/1024), across 69 layer-split cells at ctx 8192-65536 (ub 512, all kv_types). Intercept raised to cover the worst point at every context. Base_batch from 6 larger-ubatch cells. Tensor-split cells are excluded: they report one fused device whose unaccounted remainder is an artifact of that representation.

DEEPSEEK4_CSA_KV_BYTES_PER_TOKEN_LAYER_F.doc: deepseek4 compressed-sparse-attention KV bytes per token per layer at f16.
DEEPSEEK4_CSA_KV_BYTES_PER_TOKEN_LAYER_F.evidence: measured on DeepSeek-V4-Flash. Not re-fitted in this campaign; the KV term was not separated from the total.

DEFAULT_CACHE_RAM_MB.doc: llama-server's own `-cram` default: the prompt cache's cap in MiB.
DEFAULT_CACHE_RAM_MB.evidence: policy — llama.cpp's documented default, not a measurement. The cache does fill with use: 1.96 GiB of growth over 40 agent turns with -cram 8192 against 47 MiB with -cram 0 and more tokens generated.

DRAFT_MODEL_COMPUTE_MIB.doc: GPU compute buffer for a separate draft model, in MiB.
DRAFT_MODEL_COMPUTE_MIB.evidence: gemma-4-31B-QAT, the one model with a separate draft, measures a driver delta of 724, 788, and 920 MiB at ctx 32768, 65536, and 131072, and flat 724/724/728 across one, two, and four slots. Against its 107 MiB of GPU-resident draft weights and the 2 MiB per 1024 context slope, covering the worst needs 557; 620 carries roughly 8% over every measured point. Replaces 300, which modelled a flat 407 MiB total against those measurements and so under-reserved by 317 to 513 MiB at every context — the direction that OOMs, on a model the operator serves. Reachable rather than derived: one model cannot separate a per-draft weight term from a constant, so the split is asserted and only the slope is fitted.

DRAFT_MODEL_COMPUTE_MIB_PER_1K.doc: Extra GPU compute a separate MTP draft takes per 1024 tokens of context, in MiB.
DRAFT_MODEL_COMPUTE_MIB_PER_1K.evidence: driver delta across ctx 32768-131072 on the one model with a separate draft: 32768 -> 728 MiB, 65536 -> 788 MiB, 131072 -> 920 MiB. Taken from differences between contexts, which cancel the draft's weight term. Flat in the slot count, which is the control confirming the embedded head's slot scaling is its own per-slot cache.

GEMMA_E_VARIANT_BYTES_PER_LAYER_TOKEN.doc: The Gemma 4 E-variant's per-layer embedding input, charged per layer per batch token.
GEMMA_E_VARIANT_BYTES_PER_LAYER_TOKEN.evidence: 12 E-variant cells at 1027 B/layer/token, against 35 same-architecture control cells at 1. 1027 is 257 f32 elements.

IK_OP_OFFLOAD_MIN_BATCH.doc: Batch threshold below which ik keeps the MoE ops on the CPU: the term applies while `n_tokens * n_used < this * n_expert`.
IK_OP_OFFLOAD_MIN_BATCH.evidence: bracketed to (20, 32] by 50 ik MoE cells across two models with different expert counts; the term collapses from tens of MiB to hundredths exactly at the predicted crossing.

KV_CACHE_PAD.doc: llama.cpp pads the KV cache length to a multiple of this.
KV_CACHE_PAD.evidence: structural — read from llama.cpp's cache sizing, confirmed by the arena reproducing measurement to 0.1 MiB across 8 architectures.

MAINLINE_LAYER_SPLIT_MASK_COPIES.doc: How many times mainline replicates the graph's attention masks when layers are split across more than one device.
MAINLINE_LAYER_SPLIT_MASK_COPIES.evidence: 106 mainline layer-split cells at 4.00, against 149 single-card and tensor-split cells at 1.00. Flat across context, batch, slot count and cache mode; ik is 1.00 at either card count.

MAINLINE_TENSOR_MOE_BYTES_PER_NEMBD.doc: mainline's host-resident MoE intermediates under tensor split, per batch token per unit of hidden size. Multiply by n_embd for the per-token figure.
MAINLINE_TENSOR_MOE_BYTES_PER_NEMBD.evidence: 27 mainline tensor-split hybrid cells: laguna 62.7/unit, laguna 62.8/unit, qwen35moe 56.5/unit, qwen35moe 56.8/unit. Linear in batch — qwen35moe measures 28.3, 56.5, 113.0 and 226.1 MiB at ub 256, 512, 1024 and 2048, a constant rate. The same models under layer split show 0.02 MiB, so this belongs to the split mode rather than to the hybrid placement alone.

MTP_BASE_OVERHEAD_MIB.doc: The slot-independent base overhead of the MTP draft context, in MiB.
MTP_BASE_OVERHEAD_MIB.evidence: intercept of the slot sweep: Qwen3.6-27B-UD-Q5_K_ 333 oh/slot, 531 base; Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q 149 oh/slot, 371 base. The larger model's value is taken.

MTP_HOST_BYTES_EMBEDDED.doc: Host cost of an embedded multi-token-prediction head.
MTP_HOST_BYTES_EMBEDDED.evidence: 3 paired with/without cells across 2 model(s), host owned memory rather than driver VRAM. Flat in the slot count and linear in context at 1.0 MiB per 1024, so the flat constant this replaces was wrong in shape. Base covers the worst residual over every cell.

MTP_HOST_BYTES_SEPARATE_DRAFT.doc: Host cost of a separate draft GGUF for multi-token prediction.
MTP_HOST_BYTES_SEPARATE_DRAFT.evidence: 3 paired with/without cells across 1 model(s), host owned memory rather than driver VRAM. Flat in the slot count and linear in context at 1.0 MiB per 1024, so the flat constant this replaces was wrong in shape. Base covers the worst residual over every cell.

MTP_HOST_MIB_PER_1K.doc: Host memory an MTP context costs per 1024 tokens of context, in MiB.
MTP_HOST_MIB_PER_1K.evidence: the larger of the two MTP shapes' host context slopes — embedded 2, separate draft 2 MiB per 1024 tokens. One value for both, since they measure within a megabyte of each other and a second constant would claim a distinction the data does not show.

MTP_KV_INTERCEPT_MIB.doc: The constant term of the affine MTP KV model, in MiB.
MTP_KV_INTERCEPT_MIB.evidence: affine fit of mtp_context_mib against context across 2 model(s): Qwen3.6-27B-UD-Q5_K_XL 123 + 4471 B/token; Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q5_ 68 + 2504 B/token. The larger intercept is taken. The slope converges to the raw modelled KV at large contexts, so the intercept is the only correction needed.

MTP_KV_SLOPE_BYTES_PER_TOKEN.doc: The per-token slope of the affine MTP KV model, in bytes per token.
MTP_KV_SLOPE_BYTES_PER_TOKEN.evidence: per-token slope of the affine MTP KV fit across 2 model(s): Qwen3.6-27B-UD-Q5_K_XL 123 + 4471 B/token; Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q5_ 68 + 2504 B/token. The larger is taken so neither model is under-reserved.

MTP_PER_SLOT_OVERHEAD_MIB.doc: The constant per-slot overhead beyond the per-slot KV, in MiB.
MTP_PER_SLOT_OVERHEAD_MIB.evidence: per-slot overhead from the slot sweep: Qwen3.6-27B-UD-Q5_K_ 333 oh/slot, 531 base; Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q 149 oh/slot, 371 base. The larger model's value is taken.

NO_FLASH_ATTN_COMPUTE_HEAD_FACTOR.doc: Multiplier on the unfused attention score matrix when flash attention is off: the GPU compute buffer grows by this times `n_head * ctx * n_tokens * 4` bytes.
NO_FLASH_ATTN_COMPUTE_HEAD_FACTOR.evidence: measured across nine architectures at ctx 32768. Normalised by n_head x ctx x n_tokens x 4 the ratio is 1.07-1.88 for every dense and MoE architecture, so 2 covers all of them; deepseek4 sits at 0.49 because MLA shares a latent across heads, and is over-covered. Proportionality in batch is exact: qwen3 measures 2366 MiB at ub 512 and 9464 at ub 2048, and gemma3 2459 and 9884. Without this term the curves under-reserve by roughly tenfold at ub 2048 — 956 MiB reserved against 9464 taken — which is the direction that OOMs a load.

PINNED_EXTRA_BYTES.doc: Slack between the arena llama.cpp reports and the pinned memory actually resident.
PINNED_EXTRA_BYTES.evidence: n=435 cells; the modelled arena reproduces the logged figure to within 0.1 MiB on a single card for qwen3, qwen35, llama, gemma3, gemma4 (non-E), lfm2, talkie, and deepseek4, on both runtimes.

PROCESS_BASE_BYTES.doc: Fixed per-process host cost: CUDA runtime, tokenizer, sampler, graph metadata.
PROCESS_BASE_BYTES.evidence: chosen for reachability rather than fit — the measured spread across 13 models is wide enough that no single value is close to all of them, so the constant is set so every model lands inside the rolling correction's [0.8, 1.5] clamp.

PROCESS_BASE_BYTES_MOE.doc: Flat additional allowance for a mixture-of-experts model.
PROCESS_BASE_BYTES_MOE.evidence: 5 MoE models. Four of the five run as --n-cpu-moe hybrids, so MoE-ness is partly confounded with the expert-offload regime; gemma-4-26B-A4B is the only fully-offloaded control.

PROCESS_BASE_BYTES_PER_DEVICE.doc: Additional host memory per *extra* visible CUDA device, beyond the first.
PROCESS_BASE_BYTES_PER_DEVICE.evidence: measured with placement pinned to the CPU so only the CUDA context count varies: Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-U 19 MiB; gemma-3-27b-it-abliterat 20 MiB; Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q5_K_ 20 MiB going from one card to two.

PROCESS_BASE_BYTES_PER_LAYER.doc: The part of the process baseline that scales with layer count.
PROCESS_BASE_BYTES_PER_LAYER.evidence: 13 models spanning 16-79 layers. n_layer and n_embd correlate at +0.74 across the set, so the split between this term and a hidden-size term is weakly determined even though their sum is not.

QUANTISED_KV_COMPUTE_BYTES_PER_CTX_TOKEN.doc: Extra GPU compute a quantised KV cache costs, per byte of context x batch token.
QUANTISED_KV_COMPUTE_BYTES_PER_CTX_TOKEN.evidence: 32 pairs differing in nothing but the cache type, normalised by ctx x n_tokens. Rates run 0.0 to 12.3 bytes and are zero at ctx 8192 for everything and at every context for deepseek4, laguna, llama, and qwen35moe, so the worst is charged to all. Previously absorbed into the compute curves, which are fitted from the worst cell per context and did not key on cache type, so one quantised cell set the slope and every f16 service paid it.

SPEC_RECURRENT_ROLLBACK_DEPTH.doc:
Extra copies of the recurrent state a speculative-decoding service holds,
/// beyond the live one: llama.cpp's `n_rs_seq`.
SPEC_RECURRENT_ROLLBACK_DEPTH.evidence: llama.cpp's own `rs_seq` field, 3 on every speculative cell and 0 on every other, across 3 slot counts. The recurrent module is replicated `parallel x (depth + 1)`: production Qwen3.6-27B measures 1197.00 MiB against 149.62 at one slot without speculation, exactly 2 x 4.

TENSOR_MASK_BYTES_PER_TOKEN_PAIR.doc:
Bytes of KQ mask llama.cpp materialises per (batch token, cache token):
/// one f16 entry. Read from the graph, not fitted.
TENSOR_MASK_BYTES_PER_TOKEN_PAIR.evidence: every architecture measured grows by 1.00 MiB per 1024 cache tokens at ubatch 512, from talkie's 13B to gemma4's 31B, which is 2 bytes and nothing else.

hardware: 2x NVIDIA RTX 3090 (24 GiB), AMD Ryzen Threadripper 3960X (24 cores), 251 GiB RAM

ik_moe_rates.$comment: Bytes per batch token per unit of hidden size for ik's CPU-resident MoE intermediates, by architecture. `default` applies to an architecture not listed.

mtp_slot_scaling.$comment: Reported, not fitted. The MTP overhead measured at a fixed context across slot counts, which is what separates a genuine slot term from the longer context the first campaign confounded it with.
mtp_slot_scaling.observed: Qwen3.6-27B-UD-Q5_K_XL.g ctx 32768: np1 992 MiB, np2 1444 MiB, np4 2376 MiB; Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q5_K_ ctx 32768: np1 584 MiB, np2 812 MiB, np4 1224 MiB; gemma-4-31B-it-qat-UD-Q4 ctx 32768: np1 724 MiB, np2 724 MiB, np4 728 MiB

no_flash_attn_rates.$comment: Extra pinned bytes per batch token when flash attention is off, by architecture. The residual is flat in context and proportional to batch, and the rates differ fourfold between sliding-window models and the rest. `default` applies to an architecture not listed.

per_slot_host_bytes.$comment: Host memory each concurrently active slot costs, by architecture. Recorded, and deliberately not charged in `host_overhead_bytes`: that figure is what the rolling correction divides an observation by, so it must model what a process holds rather than the worst case, and charging all four slots took the cells outside the band from 2 to 44. A worst-case allowance belongs in the packer's slop, beside the prompt cache.

quantised_cache_rates.$comment: Extra pinned bytes per batch token when the KV cache is quantised, by architecture. They span a factor of forty, so one value would either under-reserve deepseek4 or over-reserve everything else by ~3 MiB. `default` applies to an architecture not listed.

tensor_compute_curves.$comment: Per-device compute buffer under `--split-mode tensor`, charged to every spanned GPU rather than divided between them: llama.cpp builds the same graph on each device, and the measured compute column reads identically on one card and on two at every context in the set. Same shape and same architecture grouping as `compute_buffer_curves`, fitted against tensor cells. An architecture absent here uses `default`.

default.evidence: least-squares fit of max per-device compute column to base + base_batch + slope*(ctx/1024), across 41 tensor-split cells at ctx 8192-65536 (ub 512, all kv_types). Intercept raised to cover the worst point at every context. Base_batch from 0 larger-ubatch cells. The unaccounted remainder is excluded and derived separately as TENSOR_SPLIT_PER_DEVICE_SHADOW_MIB: the fused device sums it across cards, so it is not a per-device figure.

entries.evidence: least-squares fit of max per-device compute column to base + base_batch + slope*(ctx/1024), across 38 tensor-split cells at ctx 8192-131072 (ub 512, all kv_types). Intercept raised to cover the worst point at every context. Base_batch from 0 larger-ubatch cells. The unaccounted remainder is excluded and derived separately as TENSOR_SPLIT_PER_DEVICE_SHADOW_MIB: the fused device sums it across cards, so it is not a per-device figure.

Intercept raised to cover the worst point at every context. Base_batch from 0 larger-ubatch cells. The unaccounted remainder is excluded and derived separately as TENSOR_SPLIT_PER_DEVICE_SHADOW_MIB: the fused device sums it across cards, so it is not a per-device figure.

least-squares fit of max per-device compute column to base + base_batch + slope*(ctx/1024), across 14 tensor-split cells at ctx 8192-131072 (ub 512, all kv_types). Intercept raised to cover the worst point at every context. Base_batch from 0 larger-ubatch cells. The unaccounted remainder is excluded and derived separately as TENSOR_SPLIT_PER_DEVICE_SHADOW_MIB: the fused device sums it across cards, so it is not a per-device figure.

least-squares fit of max per-device compute column to base + base_batch + slope*(ctx/1024), across 13 tensor-split cells at ctx 8192-65536 (ub 512, all kv_types). Intercept raised to cover the worst point at every context. Base_batch from 2 larger-ubatch cells. The unaccounted remainder is excluded and derived separately as TENSOR_SPLIT_PER_DEVICE_SHADOW_MIB: the fused device sums it across cards, so it is not a per-device figure.

tensor_compute_intermediates.$comment: n_embd-wide f32 graph intermediates a tensor split holds live per batch token, by architecture. The whole per-device compute buffer is `ubatch x (this x n_embd x 4 + 2 x n_kv + quantised_rate x context)`; the 2-byte term is the f16 KQ mask, read from the graph rather than fitted. `default` is the largest, so an unmeasured architecture over-reserves rather than OOMs.

tensor_compute_quantised_rates.$comment: Extra tensor-split compute bytes per (batch token x context token) when the KV cache is quantised, by architecture. It follows the full context, not one stream's share: Qwen3-4B shows the same absolute increase at one slot and at four. `default` is 0 because llama and talkie measure no increase at all.

tensor_compute_shadow_bytes.$comment: Per-device VRAM llama.cpp cannot attribute — CUDA context, cuBLAS workspaces, driver bookkeeping — by architecture, from single-device cells where the `unaccounted` column is still a per-device figure. Charged beside the tensor-split compute model, which excludes it.

tensor_split_baseline.$comment: Extra host baseline bytes a tensor split costs beyond a layer split, by architecture. `default` applies to an architecture not listed.
